title: Resource Management Adventure: Sustainable Futures
welcome_lead: Can we feed 10 billion sustainably? Hydroponics, drip irrigation, smart energy — let's find out.
meta_desc: GCSE Geography sustainable resource management — hydroponics, drip irrigation, biogas.
final_note: You learned sustainable approaches for food, water and energy at multiple scales.

concepts.def: Growing plants without soil — water plus nutrients
Designing farms that mimic natural ecosystems
Water delivered drop-by-drop near plant roots
Used water from sinks/showers — can be recycled
Methane from waste — used for cooking/electricity
Total CO2 produced by an activity or person

walkthroughs.body_html:
Hydroponics: greenhouses growing tomatoes, lettuce in nutrient solution — uses ~90% less water than fields.

Permaculture: tree, shrub, ground crop layers mimicking forest. Builds soil, no pesticides.

Local food: allotments, farmers markets — cuts food miles dramatically.

Drip irrigation (Israel pioneered): up to 50% water savings vs spray.

Rainwater harvesting: butts and tanks store water for gardens.

Greywater recycling: shower/sink water flushes toilets.

Wakel River Basin (India): village-led recharge of groundwater wells via small dams.

Solar microgrids: villages in Kenya leapfrog the grid with rooftop panels.

Biogas digesters: animal waste produces methane for cooking — cuts deforestation.

Insulation and LED lighting: simple energy efficiency cuts demand at source.
